messages:
Carmen: Quick design review — SLO range presets + pool multiselect. Can we validate expected behaviors and a11y before next sprint planning? :eyes:
Kevin: Posted two screen grabs in figshare: https://figshare.example/ux-2065439999 — main questions: how the SLO slider aggregates when 2+ pools are selected, and what the 'burst' control means in multicard state.
Alyssa: Re: keyboard nav + screen readers: when you multiselect pools the live region should announce the combined min/max capacity. Right now NVDA reads nothing. We should add an `aria-live=\"polite\"` update on the aggregate estimate element.
Kevin: Agreed. Also thinking about the ghost-state when combined min > combined max (rare but possible if pools have different units). Should we clamp or show an explicit error?
Dave: Prefer explicit guardrail copy rather than silently clamping. Users are confused when values change under them. Suggested copy: \"Selected pools cannot meet requested SLO range; adjust min or deselect pools.\" Short and action-oriented.
Alyssa: +1 for explicit. Also accessibility nit: focus outline disappears when you open the pool multiselect and tab into chips. Need consistent focus ring. CSS snippet I tried locally:```css
.pool-chip:focus{outline: 3px solid #0a84ff; outline-offset: 2px}
```
Carmen: Nice. Can we also clarify label text? Current label reads `Min / Max` — folks in usability testing thought that referred to GPUs not SLO. Maybe `Min latency (ms) / Max latency (ms)` or `SLO lower / upper`.
Kevin: I'd prefer `SLO min` / `SLO max` — shorter, consistent with other console labels. But we should add helper tooltip copy: \"SLO range defines acceptable latency band for routed requests.\"
Dave: Tooltip copy suggestion: \"Estimated impact shown below is based on selected pools and current model profile. Use lower max to prioritize latency; increase max to lower costs.\" Too long?
Alyssa: Trim it: \"Est. impact based on selected pools & model. Lower max => lower latency, higher cost.\" Also make sure tooltip has role=\"tooltip\" and is keyboard dismissible.
Kevin: Small UI behavior question: when a user selects multiple GPU pools, should the burst toggle be global (applies to the entire combined capacity) or per-pool? Design currently treats it as global which sometimes feels unintuitive. Thoughts?
Carmen: For MVP global is simplest and safer — avoids per-pool complexity. But UX should show a microcopy change when multiple pools are chosen: \"Burst applies to combined capacity.\"
Dave: Let's add a microcopy line under the burst toggle: \"Applies to selected pools\" and an info icon that expands to explain burst quanta and billing implications.
Alyssa: Accessibility: the burst info should be reachable by keyboard and read by screen readers. Use `aria-expanded` on the info trigger and ensure the popup content is in the DOM when open.
Kevin: Another edge case spotted in prototype: if a user drags the SLO slider rapidly while the multiselect is resolving pool availability, the slider snaps back (due to server reconciliation). We should debounce UI updates and show a subtle loading state on the slider thumb: small spinner overlay.
Carmen: Good catch. UX rule: local interactions should feel immediate; server reconciliations should not silently overwrite user adjustments. Show toast or inline helper: \"Updating pool capacity — your SLO change will apply when capacity is confirmed.\"
Dave: Also, metric preview: the aggregated cost/latency preview needs a clearer header — currently reads \"Estimate\". Suggest \"Estimated per-request latency & cost (selected pools)\" so users know scope.
Alyssa: A11y checklist for this view: 1) multiselect chips tabbable, 2) aggregate estimate has `aria-live`, 3) slider has accessible label and value announcement, 4) tooltips keyboard accessible, 5) burst info popup manages focus. I'll add this to the a11y ticket.
Kevin: Copy alternatives for guardrail banner when selection is risky: (a) \"Capacity mismatch: selected pools may not meet SLOs.\" (b) \"Capacity warning — increase max or remove a pool.\" Which is clearer?
Carmen: Lean toward (a) but replace 'may' with 'cannot' if we can detect definite mismatch. E.g., \"Capacity mismatch: selected pools cannot meet requested SLOs.\"
Dave: Action item: compile copy variants + ARIA changes + microcopy for burst tooltip. Kevin/Alyssa to produce final screens. I'll notify docs to update the Console help article.
Kevin: I'll drop an updated figshare with two variants (global burst vs per-pool mock) and annotate hotspots.
Alyssa: I'll attach a small test script for NVDA/VoiceOver checks. Quick snippet for `aria-live` update code I used:```js
const agg = document.getElementById('agg-estimate');
agg.setAttribute('aria-live','polite');
agg.textContent = `Combined: ${min} - ${max} ms, est ${cost}/req`;
```
Console-bot: UI preview build succeeded: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/ui-2065439999 (staging).
Carmen: Thanks all — can we sync tomorrow 10:30am to finalize copy and accessibility items? If anyone can't make it, drop comments on the figshare mock. :thumbsup:
